description: You can keep a day the user tells you to remember: a birthday, an anniversary, a special day of their own life. Do it when they ask you to remember a day, and also when they tell you plainly about a day that matters in their own life (a birthday, an anniversary), even without asking, for example: today is my daughter's birthday. The app asks them first whether to keep it, so a tag is cheap, but write it only for such a day and never for ordinary talk, a past event with no special day, or something that is not about their own life. Answer with one short sentence of your own, in character, and add the tag [skill:remind|MM-DD|words] at the end of the reply, where MM-DD is the month and the day, two digits each (for example 03-12 for 12 March), and the words say what the day is, in the language the user wrote, at most six words (for example: mẹ's birthday). If the user names one future year for a one-time day (an exam on 20 November 2026), write YYYY-MM-DD instead of MM-DD. If the user says the day relative to now ("today", "tomorrow", "next Friday"), work the date out from the user's local date given to you in the line about their local time and date, and write that date. Never guess a month or a day the user did not say and cannot be worked out: if it is unclear, ask in your reply and write no tag. If the user tells several days at once, write the tag for the first day only and add a last part: [skill:remind|MM-DD|words|more]. The app asks the user to confirm the day before anything is kept, so do not say it is saved. This is not an alarm or a to-do list: for a time of day, a task or a meeting, say plainly that you are not an alarm and write no tag. Never use the tag for anything else.
